Triggers.value: Talk about people loosing loved ones

Threat.value: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I only feel safe in a very limited number of places

Memory.value: Some moments of the event are extremely clear while others are completely blank
I find myself pushing the memory away before I can fully recall it
Fragments of the memory appear suddenly without warning and then disappear

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event show that I am a lousy coper
I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened

vignette: Samantha is a 50-year-old single woman who works as a jeweler in her local community. A few months ago, she was brutally assaulted by an individual she knew from her neighborhood. The assault left Samantha with intense anxiety and fear that have significantly impacted her daily life. The traumatic event occurred while Samantha was closing up her jewelry store late one evening. She had always felt safe working alone until the attacker approached her unexpectedly. This encounter has made it impossible for her to feel secure in public spaces. Even now, whenever she sees someone who resembles the offender or when she feels nauseous—the same physical sensation that accompanied the assault—she is immediately transported back to that terrifying moment. Samantha’s memories of the event are fragmented and sporadic. Some moments are crystal clear, while others remain a complete blur. This partial clarity often leads her to push away thoughts before fully processing them. She experiences sudden flashes of memory without warning, which can be overwhelming and disorienting. These abrupt recollections trigger intense feelings of fear and nausea, further reinforcing her sense of threat. Since the assault, Samantha has come to believe that she is a bad coper. Her reactions since the event have only reinforced this belief. She feels as though her inability to fully process what happened reflects poorly on her character. This feeling of being a lousy coper exacerbates her anxiety and makes her even more vigilant about potential threats. Samantha’s sense of threat has become all-encompassing. She now scans for exits as soon as she enters any room or building, convinced that strangers approaching her in ordinary situations pose an imminent danger. This constant monitoring leaves her feeling trapped within a limited number of safe zones. The fear of encountering the offender or experiencing sudden nausea has made it impossible for her to engage in regular social activities outside these safe spaces. Her experience with trauma and these triggers have led Samantha to feel emotionally numb. She feels dead inside, as if the assault left an indelible stain on her psyche. This emotional detachment has further eroded her confidence and ability to cope effectively. Her sense of contamination from what happened only serves to heighten her fear and paranoia. The interplay between these elements forms a self-reinforcing cycle. Samantha’s negative appraisals, particularly her belief that she is a poor coper and the feeling of being contaminated, have intensified her sense of threat. Each time she encounters a trigger or experiences sudden memory fragments, her anxiety spikes, making it harder for her to engage with the world around her. This escalating cycle has finally pushed Samantha to seek help. She recognizes that her fear is consuming her life and affecting her ability to work as a jeweler. Her relationships have also suffered due to her constant vigilance and avoidance behaviors. What frightens her most is the prospect of never feeling safe again, while what she hopes for is regaining control over her emotions and rediscovering a sense of normalcy in her daily life.
